briefing.opening: Good day. Welcome to the Climate Change Daily Briefing for November 26, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 [Global Crisis] Unprecedented Streak Above 2°C and the Breakdown of COP31 Negotiations
sections.content: An unprecedented climate crisis has become reality as global average temperatures exceeded pre-industrial levels by more than 2°C for six consecutive days for the first time in recorded history [11]. With the international community failing to reach consensus on climate action, record-breaking temperature surges observed in November have further heightened global alarm [134]. Meanwhile, the recent 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) negotiations ultimately collapsed, triggering fierce blame-shifting and severe geopolitical fallout [9, 139]. Observers on the ground delivered sobering assessments that climate risks are now unequivocally outpacing the speed of global response [131].

sections.title: 🌱 [Domestic Innovation] Jeju Declares '2035 Carbon Neutrality Vision'… Striving for 100% Renewable Energy
sections.content: Jeju Special Self-Governing Province has officially declared its '2035 Carbon Neutrality Vision,' setting a target to transition 100% of the island's energy generation to renewables and phase out thermal power generation by 2035 [13, 25, 75]. To achieve this, the province plans to add 5.5 GW of solar and wind capacity, ensure 100% of newly registered vehicles are electric from 2030, and deploy 200,000 heat pumps [46, 80, 114]. In addition, partnering with Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO), Jeju is introducing the 'Tamna Electricity Forecast,' which offers electricity discounts of up to 50% during daytime hours when surplus renewable power is generated, aiming to transform power consumption patterns [94, 99, 108]. Jeju is thus emerging as a living laboratory for green civilization, linking power market reform directly to resident income generation [62, 71, 85].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 [Industry & Policy] Overhaul of Carbon-Neutral Tech Roadmap and Semiconductor Renewable Energy Challenges
sections.content: The government has restructured its carbon neutrality roadmap to secure technologies capable of halving national greenhouse gas emissions, expanding its scope to encompass climate change adaptation [5, 12]. Notably, the newly unveiled comprehensive technology innovation roadmap drew policy attention for excluding the nuclear energy sector [16]. Meanwhile, within the industrial sector, the fact that over 80% of carbon emissions from semiconductor manufacturing stem from electricity consumption has emerged as a central issue [73, 86, 91]. Industry bodies, including SEMI, underscored that scaling up renewable energy supplies across Asia and establishing a predictable market environment are urgent prerequisites for semiconductor decarbonization [76, 91].

sections.title: ⚠️ [International Warnings] Accelerating Climate Disasters and Risks of Infrastructure and Ecosystem Loss
sections.content: In the United Kingdom, where extreme summer heatwaves caused more than 5,000 deaths, approximately 100 Labour MPs submitted a letter urging the rejection of the Rosebank oilfield development and demanding an end to fossil fuel expansion [142]. Additionally, Denmark's central bank warned of surging storm surge risks and mounting potential financial sector losses driven by climate change [136]. Compounding these concerns, academic analyses revealed that peatland drainage accounts for several percent of global warming drivers, while warnings also emerged that under current policies, Australia will achieve only a 48% emissions reduction by 2035, falling well short of its 62–70% target [113, 118].

briefing.closing: Even amid rising global temperatures and stalled international climate negotiations, bold regional energy transitions and policy reform efforts are actively taking shape. This concludes the Climate Briefing for November 26, 2026.
